title: Does Industry Employment of Active Regulators Weaken Oversight?
eligible_reason: Tables 4-6 report, for each of three outcomes and three treatment definitions, a column with no controls: reghdfe outcome treat, absorb(i.fyear##i.sic2 i.gvkey) cluster(gvkey). The treatment is a binary indicator that switches on in the firm-specific year an active FREP executive joins the firm's board (appointment years spread over 2004-2018 across 28 treated firms), firm FE plus industry-by-year FE (a time-invariant characteristic interacted with calendar time, allowed), several hundred never-treated German firms, linear estimation. Post-tenure years are dropped (set to missing), which matches the protocol's treatment of switch-offs.
design_notes: Firm-year panel of German listed non-financial firms from Compustat Global (samplems.dta: 21,167 firm-years, 1,450 firms, fyear 1987-2019; analysis fyear>2003, ~697 firms after dropping missing controls and singletons per README). Outcomes built in the do-file: errorfyear (FREP enforcement action for the misstated year, from the Federal Gazette; 158 flagged firm-years in the raw file), audproblem from auop, highriskf1 from a Dechow F-score formula, tacc (accruals). Treatments treatheadten / treatnonom / treatboardtena hand-coded by gvkey and year (28 treated firms, 137 treated firm-years per README). Each table: columns (1),(3),(5) without controls, (2),(4),(6) with laglogat lagroa leverage lagmtb ma big4 (winsorized per sample). FE absorb(i.fyear##i.sic2 i.gvkey), cluster gvkey. Table 7 accruals with Jones-model controls; Table 8 interactions; Table 9 SEC comment letters (cross-listed firms); Tables 10-12 determinants/directorships.
n_adoption_cohorts: about 12 distinct appointment years (first treated fiscal year 2004-2018 depending on treatment definition; e.g. treatboardtena: 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: read from the hand-coded replace statements in code final.do; exact cohort counts should be recomputed after running the treatment-coding block
always_treated_note: DMG Mori (gvkey 101937) coded treated from 2003, i.e. from the start of the fyear>2003 window

specs.treatment_definition: any FREP senior executive (Head of Enforcement, board member or Nomination Committee member) sits on the firm's board during their FREP tenure; coded by hand per gvkey and fiscal year in 'code final.do' lines 260-387 (post-tenure years set to missing, i.e. dropped; Deutsche Post 2011-2017 coded 0 between two spells)
specs.fe: gvkey + fyear + sic2 + fyear#sic2 (absorb(i.fyear##i.sic2 i.gvkey)): firm FE and two-digit-industry-by-year FE
specs.sample_condition: insnnn==1: German non-financial listed firms (Compustat Global, fic==DEU, SIC not 6000-6999), fyear>2003, firm-years with non-missing controls (e(sample) of the controls regression at lines 392-398), singletons dropped by reghdfe
specs.reported_location: Table 4, column (1) (the adjacent column adds controls laglogat lagroa leverage lagmtb ma big4 and is excluded)
specs.notes: Treatment switches off when the FREP executive leaves the board; the author sets most post-tenure years to missing (dropped), consistent with Hull footnote 6; for Deutsche Post (gvkey 241456) the gap years 2011-2017 are coded 0 and should be dropped under the protocol. sic2 is built from sich (historical SIC) when available, so a few firms may change industry over time.

data_provenance: real (Compustat Global extract plus hand-collected FREP enforcement and directorship data, shipped as .dta)
software_notes: Stata reghdfe, winsor; single do-file builds variables, treatments and all tables.
screener_notes: Treated group is small (28 firms, 137 firm-years), so the leverage screen (effective clusters, max cluster share) matters. Treatment construction must be replicated by executing lines 139-387 of code final.do (pure data edits, safe to port). Column numbering within Tables 4-6 inferred from code order (treatboardtena, treatnonom, treatheadten; no-controls column first). Screened from package only.
